topics: Timeline and success criteria for pilot
transcript:
00:00:00 - Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, happy New Years eve, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep to 45. Quick roll call?
00:00:08 - Sarah Kim: Hi Sarah here, Sarah Kim from NexaHealth.
00:00:11 - Daniel Lee: Daniel, infra.
00:00:13 - Priya Reddy: Priya, security.
00:00:15 - Tom Brooks: Tom, product.
00:00:18 - Marco Diaz: Marco from Redwood, SE.
00:00:20 - Aisha Patel: Great. Quick agenda, onboarding status, environment access, mini-benchmark plan, security follow-ups, then action items.
00:00:33 - Sarah Kim: Sounds good. On our side we completed the initial API key exchange, we have a test dataset uploaded to our S3 dev bucket, but the VPC peering is still blocked by our network team because they need the exact CIDRs and a diagram.
00:00:45 - Aisha Patel: OK that matches what Daniel mentioned in the notes. Daniel, what do you need from us to unblock?
00:00:50 - Daniel Lee: If you can give us the peering CIDR ranges and the port list we need to open, then the ticket will move. Also we need confirmation on whether the Redwood private deployment requires a private route or if NAT egress is OK, there's some policy differences.
00:01:05 - Marco Diaz: For the pilot we can do either but recommended is VPC peering for lowest latency. We'll provide the CIDRs; Redwood public docs sometimes say 10.10.0.0/16 in examples, but we'll give you the exact ranges for the Dedicated pool if you're doing private.
00:01:20 - Priya Reddy: Security question: KMS integration, where are keys stored, can they be customer-managed? Also audit logs - we need retention policy details.
00:01:28 - Aisha Patel: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in our Private deployment; for Hosted there is an option to integrate with your KMS via a customer-managed key, but there are some limitations on rotation windows. We'll put the specifics in the security pack. For audit logs we keep request/response metadata for 30 days by default and can extend for enterprise.
00:01:45 - Tom Brooks: For success criteria, we said <100ms p50 on our typical single-turn prompts and cost under $0.001 per token equivalent - is that still realistic?
00:01:54 - Marco Diaz: The latency target is achievable on Dedicated with the model variants we've discussed, p50 of 80-110ms depending on sequence length. Cost per token will vary; our Optimize suggestions (batching + caching + quant) can reduce unit cost by ~30% in many cases.
00:02:10 - Sarah Kim: Great. Can you run a benchmark on our sample data? We'll share a 1k query set.
00:02:15 - Marco Diaz: Yes, plan is to run a 1k run at simulated concurrency levels (1, 5, 10), measure p50/p95 and token cost. We'll push the results and the raw traces. Aim to have that by next week.
00:02:26 - Daniel Lee: About network - do you need egress rules for S3 or does Redwood pull from S3? How do you ingest the sample dataset?
00:02:33 - Aisha Patel: Typical pattern is we request access to the S3 presigned URLs or a temporary IAM role; for the private deploy we can also mount a transfer endpoint. We'll detail options in the onboarding checklist.
00:02:45 - Priya Reddy: Also need to confirm SSO/SAML flows and RBAC roles. For pilot we only need developer-level access but we want the production roles map.
00:02:55 - Lena Zhou: (CSM) We'll send the SSO/SAML mapping doc; Redwood supports SCIM provisioning and we have example role mappings.
00:03:03 - Sarah Kim: One small transcription/mis-say: our compliance team asked whether request payloads are stored; you said metadata only, but want that in writing.
00:03:11 - Aisha Patel: Correct, by default we store request/response metadata for observability; payload retention is opt-in and can be disabled. We'll include the exact policy in the security pack and the contract addendum.
00:03:25 - Marco Diaz: Quick technical note: when we run the mini-bench we'll use a quantized variant to reflect production cost profiles, and we'll run with KV caching enabled for repeated prefixes if your workload has reuse. If you have long context sizes we might recommend a different kernel selection.
00:03:41 - Tom Brooks: Our average prompt length is around 160 tokens, but we have a long tail with some 1k token contexts.
00:03:47 - Marco Diaz: That helps. We'll include p50/p95 across the length buckets.
00:03:52 - Daniel Lee: About infra, if we want to run Redwood Private on-prem, what's the timeline and infra requirements? We're evaluating both Hosted pilot and an eventual Private path.
00:04:00 - Aisha Patel: Private typically requires a minimum of N GPUs and a private control plane; for a pilot we can do a small footprint, but full production we'd size to your throughput. We'll share the infra recipe; for early proof-of-concept Hosted or Dedicated is faster to stand up.
00:04:14 - Priya Reddy: Any SOC2/ISO artifacts we can see now?
00:04:18 - Aisha Patel: Yes we'll share the security pack including SOC2 attestation, ISO certs, pen test summary, and the KMS/Audit docs.
00:04:26 - Sarah Kim: Awesome.
00:04:28 - Aisha Patel: Ok let's recap action items: Redwood to send onboarding checklist and CIDR ranges; Marco to run benchmark; Nexa to provide VPC details and sample dataset access; Priya to confirm compliance questions and we'll follow up.
00:04:40 - Daniel Lee: I'll open the ticket after I get the CIDRs.
00:04:42 - Aisha Patel: Great, thanks everyone. We'll schedule a brief 20 minute follow-up next Friday to review benchmarks. Happy holidays.
00:04:49 - Sarah Kim: Thanks all.
00:04:51 - (call ends)
references: Sample dataset S3 bucket - details in private chat
notes: Crosstalk and occasional transcription errors: 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'k-c cache'; 'quantization' appears as 'quantize shun' in auto transcript. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated for pilot but open to Hosted if we can meet latency targets.
